events.title: 20th Annual AICA-USA Kippy Stroud Distinguished Critic Lecture: Saidiya Hartman
events.blurb: Scholar and writer Saidiya Hartman delivers the twentieth annual Kippy Stroud Distinguished Critic Lecture on contemporary art criticism, co-presented with the Vera List Center.

events.title: Current Work | Forms of Intelligence: Labor
events.venue: Frederick P. Rose Auditorium, The Cooper Union
events.blurb: Architectural League lecture examining how artificial intelligence and automated workflows reshape architectural practice, studio production, and what forms of design labor remain human.

events.title: Paulina Sawczuk: Design as an Encounter — Between Context, Culture and Place
events.venue: The Cooper Union — Civic Projects Lab
events.blurb: Finnish architect and product designer Paulina Sawczuk presents two international projects on participatory design, equity, and cross-disciplinary collaboration beyond spatial form.

events.title: What Happened to Video Art?: A Symposium on Artists' Moving Images
events.blurb: Full-day symposium with Anton Vidokle, Martha Rosler, Rachel Rose, Paul Pfeiffer, and Peggy Ahwesh tracing how projection technologies and museums reshaped artists' moving-image work.

events.title: Visible and Invisible Hands: Romana Schmalisch & Robert Schlicht
events.blurb: Screening of Labour Power Plant and The Choreography of Commodities followed by a discussion with Berlin filmmakers Romana Schmalisch and Robert Schlicht on automated ports and shipping.

events.title: Jan Wilker for Open Flat File
events.venue: Frederick P. Rose Auditorium, The Cooper Union
events.blurb: Designer Jan Wilker lectures on Karl Gerstner's Think Program and morphological boxes for the Herb Lubalin Study Center, with free commemorative posters distributed to attendees.

events.title: War Trash
events.venue: The New School — Starr Foundation Hall
events.address: 63 Fifth Ave, Lower Level, New York, NY 10003
events.blurb: Afternoon symposium organized with SculptureCenter around Aziz Hazara's Coming Home exhibition, examining military supply chains, salvaged equipment, and the material aftermath of occupation.

events.title: Counterfictional Futures: Speculations On Biological Intelligence
events.address: 120 Walker St, Fl 3 & 4, New York, NY 10013
events.blurb: Office of Applied Strategy launches Dossier 3 with an author discussion on biological intelligence, open-source seed printing, and speculative social foresight.

events.title: Księżyc
events.blurb: Polish avant-folk ensemble Księżyc and multi-instrumentalist Paweł Romańczuk perform acoustic vocal and minimalist chamber music in the Main Hall with Unsound Festival.

events.title: Unruly Play
events.address: 120 Walker St, Fl 3 & 4, New York, NY 10013
events.blurb: Studio Imagination of Things presents an archive of unconventional urban games and leads a participatory evening of live spatial play mechanics.

events.title: Breaking Walled Gardens
events.blurb: Hands-on iOS jailbreaking and permacomputing workshop guiding participants through unlocking legacy Apple hardware to extend device lifespans and reduce e-waste.

events.title: Counterfictional Futures: Speculations On Machine Intelligence
events.blurb: Second Dossier 3 book launch session hosted by Tony Wang, examining speculative design scenarios and cultural consequences around autonomous machine intelligence.

events.title: The Infinite Wager: Risk, Uncertainty, and the Philosophy of Predictive Tech
events.blurb: Interactive seminar led by Emma Stamm analyzing prediction markets, probabilistic forecasting systems, and the philosophical assumptions behind predictive computation.

events.title: Book Launch | Nolan Oswald Dennis: Ecliptics
events.blurb: Monograph launch with Nolan Oswald Dennis, Zoë Hopkins, and KJ Abudu featuring a collective reading and diagramming session rooted in Dennis's Black Earth Study Club.

events.title: Press Play 2026
events.blurb: Two-day small-press book, zine, record, and artist-ephemera fair filling the Red Hook hall with tables from over 130 independent publishers, talks, and workshops.

events.title: Ellis & Parker von Sternberg: Normativity
events.blurb: Full-scale curved sectional sofa sculptures built from fiberglass, foam, metal, leather, and faux leather fill the Henry Street storefront with uncanny domestic furniture forms.

events.title: Dani McKenzie: A Puff of Smoke
events.blurb: Thirteen oil paintings on linen and board frame nocturnal New York apartment windows, fire escapes, and lit interiors observed from across the street.

events.title: Wretched Mirror
events.blurb: Eighteen-artist group show including Lynn Hershman Leeson, Martha Rosler, Laurie Simmons, and Nikita Gale presenting domestic objects, photography, and sculptures twisted by subtle distortion.

events.title: Break Up
events.blurb: Thirteen-artist group exhibition of paintings and small sculptural works marking Essex Flowers' final show at its 19 Monroe Street space after ten years.

events.title: Scott Lyall: REDS
events.blurb: Six monochrome inkjet paintings paired with four small cast glass objects investigate digital color models, optical perception, and algorithmic image making.

events.title: Beatriz Zamora: The Lost Works
events.blurb: Recovered late-1970s textured black monochrome paintings by Mexican artist Beatriz Zamora, brought from Mexico City in 1980 and shown in New York for the first time.

events.title: Pattern Recognition: Superhouse at Five
events.address: 120 Walker St, 3rd Fl, New York, NY 10013
events.blurb: Fifth-anniversary exhibition assembling unseen archival and studio art furniture, cabinetry, textiles, and sculptural objects by 21 makers including Aspen Golann, Liz Collins, and Dan Friedman.

events.title: Misha Kahn: All Intensive Purposes
events.blurb: Experimental furniture and cast-metal dining tables, glass vessels, onyx forms, and woven objects built from spontaneous material improvisations and folded paper studies.

events.title: Katie Stout: Fly Trap
events.blurb: Clocks, mirrors, and sculptural lighting fixtures by Katie Stout crafted in mixed ornament and patinated surfaces to trace accumulation, decay, and passing time.

events.title: Jos Devriendt: Terra Sigillata
events.blurb: Over twenty ceramic mushroom lamps from Belgian designer Jos Devriendt's Night & Day series finished in fine terra sigillata clay slips for smooth, mineral-colored surfaces.

events.title: Alexandre de Betak: Truss Light Sculptures 01
events.blurb: Twelve aluminum and bronze light sculptures across two rooms repurposing industrial stage trusses and theatrical luminaires into freestanding architectural fixtures.

events.title: No Ordinary Light: Akari at 75
events.blurb: Survey of Isamu Noguchi's collapsible washi paper and bamboo wire-base Akari light sculptures installed alongside stone, metal, and clay works across the museum.

events.title: LaJuné McMillian: To See for Oneself
events.blurb: Interactive worldbuilding installation combining custom motion-based software, living ecological systems, and meditative spatial environments by new-media artist LaJuné McMillian.

events.title: Cevdet Erek: Americas
events.address: 44-19 Purves St, Long Island City, NY 11101
events.blurb: Site-specific sonic architecture built from steel and iron fencing, wooden sticks, amplifiers, and computer-driven three-channel rhythmic sound.

events.title: Elmgreen & Dragset: TRANSITION
events.blurb: Monumental nearly full-scale model of the White House Oval Office fabricated in weathered corten steel, paired with wall-mounted Balcony Series architectural sculptures.

events.title: Lucas Samaras: Boxes and Reconstructions
events.blurb: Intricate mixed-media box assemblages studded with pins, mirrors, and found objects alongside previously unexhibited 1979 stitched fabric Reconstructions.

events.title: Wade Guyton: Sculpture
events.blurb: Multi-part sculptures in cast bronze, painted cast aluminum, stainless steel, plaster, and Douglas fir paired with large inkjet-printed linen panels.

events.title: UrbanSparkle 2026
events.blurb: Annual wearable-glass jewelry exhibition uniting enamel and metalsmithing techniques in new pieces by Danielle Embry, Meghan Schmiedel, Myriam Saavedra, and Tanya Crane.
events.hours: Tue–Sat 11 AM–7 PM, Sun 11 AM–5 PM

events.title: FAD Market: Holiday Pop-Up at Empire Stores
events.blurb: Daily indie makers market inside the Dumbo waterfront warehouse with rotating weekend rosters of studio jewelers, ceramicists, and metalworkers.

events.title: Hot Glass Hangout & Studio Sale with Shuhei Fujii
events.blurb: First Friday molten-glassblowing demonstration by Shuhei Fujii paired with a pop-up studio sale of handmade glass jewelry and vessels by UrbanGlass resident artists.

events.title: Renegade Craft Fair — New York Winter
events.blurb: Two-day indoor winter market in Chelsea bringing together over 200 independent jewelry designers, studio metalsmiths, ceramicists, and small-batch object makers.

events.title: Open Studios: Winter in the City
events.blurb: Afternoon open studio inside UrbanGlass's 17,000-square-foot facility featuring live glassblowing, flameworked beadmaking, fusing, and neon-bending demonstrations.
